subject: Switchability, cost certainty, and integration snapshot
messages:
From: Nate Johnson <nate@orchid.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samantha Lee <samantha.proc@orchid.ai>
Date: 2026-10-18T09:21:00-07:00
Subject: Vendor comparison: pricing + integration questions

Hi Rachel / Jordan —

Thanks for taking the time yesterday. Our procurement team asked for a concise comparison between Redwood and the other vendor (EdgeCloud) on three fronts before we present to execs next week: 1) firm unit economics and any one-time credits you can offer, 2) migration friction (how long, blockers, what we ship), and 3) integration surface (KMS, VPC peering, audit logs).

EdgeCloud gave us a 12-month pilot at 40% off for the first quarter + a managed migration credit. They also committed to a two-week proof-of-concept where they'd deploy a mirrored inference stack.

Can you send a short deliverable we can use in the Exec packet (1 page econ, 1 page integration checklist)? Also flag any must-have pre-reqs on our side.

Samantha is on procurement — looping her for logistics.

Thanks,
Nate
Nate Johnson
VP of Engineering, Orchid AI
N: (415) 555-0124

Attachments: (none)
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Nate Johnson <nate@orchid.ai>, Samantha Lee <samantha.proc@orchid.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-18T12:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Vendor comparison: pricing + integration questions

Nate / Samantha —

Appreciate the context. I put together a two-pager that directly answers the three bullets you called out and a short counterproposal that balances price with predictable latency and an ops handoff. High level:
- Pricing: we can offer a targeted pilot package — 3 months at 35% off + a $25k migration credit toward dedicated capacity if you commit to a 12-month reserved plan.
- Migration friction: typical mirrored POC takes 2–3 weeks (we'll provide the deployment playbook + engineer hours). Full migration depends on your integration surface (KV cache persistence, model quantization alignment) — I included a checklist.
- Integration: we support VPC peering, customer-managed KMS, audit logs (S3 + CloudTrail integration), and a private agent for on-prem gating.

Attaching: redwood_switch_econ_sheet.xlsx (econ model), orchid_onboard_checklist.pdf (integration items), integration_runbook_v1.docx (deployment playbook).

If you want stronger price alignment with EdgeCloud's intro numbers, we can structure a phased credit — e.g., an additional one-time credit if you commit to a tiered runway (details in the econ sheet). I'm happy to turn this into the one-pager for your packet; do you prefer concise bullets or an annotated slide?

I'll loop in Karthik for a quick tech note on quantization/latency considerations.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_switch_econ_sheet.xlsx; orchid_onboard_checklist.pdf; integration_runbook_v1.docx

Subject: Re: Vendor comparison: pricing + integration questions

Rachel —

Thanks for the materials, they look thorough. Quick follow-ups from procurement: EdgeCloud's 40% off + managed migration credit reduces our near-term cash outlay and gives us a clearly time-boxed mirroring window. Two asks before we can recommend Redwood to the execs: 1) can you match the effective introductory discount for the first quarter (EdgeCloud's math yields ~40% off token unit pricing for Q1), and 2) can you confirm a hard SLA for the pilot environment (latency p95 target and uptime)?

Also Nate flagged the integration checklist: what parts require network changes that would need our security team's approval (they're sensitive about new VPC peering and cross-account KMS).

If it's easier, can you propose two concrete concession options we can show the execs (e.g., A: 40% Q1 + smaller migration credit; B: 30% Q1 + larger migration/staging credit + guaranteed one-week remediation SLA)?

Samantha
Director, Procurement, Orchid AI
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.proc@orchid.ai>, Nate Johnson <nate@orchid.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-19T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Vendor comparison: pricing + integration questions

Samantha / Nate —

Thanks — below are two clean options you can present to execs. I kept tradeoffs explicit so procurement and engineering know the operational consequences.

Option A — Aggressive intro (EdgeCloud parity):
- Commercial: 40% off token rates for months 0–3 (pilot), then revert to standard hosted tiers unless you convert to a reserved Dedicated plan.
- Credit: $15k one-time migration credit applied to onboarding invoice.
- SLA: pilot environment p95 latency target documented at 220ms for the sample workload you shared; 99.5% availability for pilot. Remediation SLAs apply (see runbook).
- Tradeoffs: short runway on volume discounts; pilot egress and burst caps are tighter. Requires a written conversion commitment window to redeem additional credits.

Option B — Stability-weighted (lower upfront discount, stronger migration support):
- Commercial: 30% off token rates for months 0–3 + $40k migration credit toward Dedicated commit or implementation hours if you sign 12-month reserved capacity within 90 days.
- Credit: applied as a credit or as dedicated-engineer time (you choose).
- SLA: pilot p95 latency target 200ms (optimized routes + KV cache tuning); 99.9% availability; 4-hour initial remediation SLA during business hours for pilot (1-week guaranteed remediation window for critical incidents if Dedicated commit is signed).
- Tradeoffs: slightly higher near-term unit cost but much lower ops risk and prioritized migration support. Better for teams prioritizing low-latency SLAs at go-live.

Network/security notes (Karthik):
- VPC peering: we can do VPC peering or PrivateLink depending on your cloud; peering requires a short security review but no host-level access.
- KMS: we support customer-managed KMS keys; key grants need an IAM role trust established (standard 2–3 day security ops window).
- Audit logs: we stream request/response metadata to your S3 + CloudTrail; no customer data is persisted outside your controlled buckets unless you opt into shared caching for cost reasons.

Next steps I recommend:
1) Tell us which option (A or B) you want in the exec packet; we will tighten wording and produce a single-slide summary.
2) If you pick B, we will provision a pilot environment with dedicated on-call hours and an on-site review (if needed).
3) Karthik can run a 30-minute security call with your SecOps to get the KMS/peering checklist cleared.

I'll prepare the slide and updated econ sheet depending on your choice.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

If helpful, I can add a single line tying the migration credit to measurable cutover checkpoints (dry run, mirrored traffic, cutover).
